rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that some items must be created first as tools or prerequisites, and those tools are then needed to obtain other items during an ongoing collection process: Model a task for each stated creation step, named with the verb and object from the description, placed in the process before the step that obtains the dependent items resumes. Connect it with sequence flows so the dependent collection cannot proceed until the prerequisite task is complete. Do not fold the creation into the gathering task or drop it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that some items must be created first as tools or prerequisites, and those tools are then needed to obtain other items during an ongoing collection process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an interrupting occurrence sets an ongoing work step back and that the same work step is then carried on or continued afterwards: Model the recovery from the interruption as its own task, and model the continued work as a separate task placed after it, connected by a sequence flow. Label the continuation task with the verb and main object the description uses for the continued work, not with the name of the recovery.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an interrupting occurrence sets an ongoing work step back and that the same work step is then carried on or continued afterwards

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names two distinct responsible parties, a human user who makes the choices and an automated component that carries out the later work, and both are needed in the same process: Model the process as one participant pool with one lane per named responsible party (a lane for the user and a separate lane for the automated component). Place each activity and event in the lane of the party that performs it: the user's initiating event and choice-gathering steps in the user lane, and the autonomous execution step in the automated component's lane. Do not omit these lanes, and do not put the automated work in a start event; model the work as a task in the automated lane.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names two distinct responsible parties, a human user who makes the choices and an automated component that carries out the later work, and both are needed in the same process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a person must first choose or specify which items are wanted, and only after that choice does an automated process begin: Model a bpmn:userTask for that human selection step, placed as an activity before the first automated task, and connect it by sequence flow so the automated work cannot start until the selection is complete. Do not omit the selection step or let the automated process start without it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a person must first choose or specify which items are wanted, and only after that choice does an automated process begin

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that once a set of preparations or preferences is complete, an activity begins within the same process, and that start is not stated as the trigger of the whole process: Model that beginning as a bpmn:task placed after the completion decision and connected by a sequence flow. Do not model it as a new bpmn:startEvent, and do not split the process into a second start. Reserve bpmn:startEvent for the stated trigger of the whole process.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that once a set of preparations or preferences is complete, an activity begins within the same process, and that start is not stated as the trigger of the whole process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several activities performed by one actor in a comma-separated sequence, states no ordering or dependency among them, and then a later activity is described as following all of them: Model the listed activities as parallel branches: fork them from the preceding step with a parallel gateway, and join them with a parallel gateway before the later activity, so the later activity waits for all branches. Do not chain the unordered activities in a fixed sequence unless the description states an order.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description states that an activity can be carried out for several items at the same time, up to a stated maximum number, and gives no order among the items before a later step follows.
